statement: Reduction of Levels: CMMC 2.0 reduces the number of certification levels from five to three:

cmmc_1_0: Level 1: Third-party assessment Level 2: N/A Level 3: Third-party assessment Level 4: N/A Level 5: Third-party assessment
cmmc_2_0: Level 1: Annual self-assessment Level 2: Triennial third-party assessment for critical national security information, annual self-assessment for other information Level 3: Triennial government-led assessment
statement: Self-Assessment and Third-Party Assessments: CMMC 1.0 required third-party assessment starting at Level 1. CMMC 2.0 allows for self-assessment for Level 1 and, in some cases, Level 2.

cmmc_1_0: Not explicitly tied to NIST SP 800-171
cmmc_2_0: Directly aligned with NIST SP 800-171 and a subset of NIST SP 800-172
statement: NIST SP 800-171 Alignment: CMMC 2.0 closely aligns with NIST SP 800-171r2 standards for protecting CUI.
Eliminates CMMC 1.0 Levels 2 and Levels 4; these levels were originally intended as transition levels and not meant to be assessed requirements

feature: Eliminated unique practices and maturity processes
cmmc_1_0: CMMC unique practices and maturity processes
statement: Eliminates all CMMC unique practices and maturity processes; works with NIST to address identified gaps in NIST SP 800-171

CMMC 2.0 also allows for “Plan of Action and Milestone” reports, otherwise known as PoAMs. These can be used by contractors that currently don't meet the security requirements. This allows them to continue to bid on DoD contracts, provided they also submit an outline of how they will implement security procedures in the future.
